newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican guerrillas claim mainland bombing.
newsitem.headline: Corsican guerrillas claim mainland bombing.

text.p: A clandestine Corsican separatist movement claimed responsibility on Monday for a weekend bomb attack outside a court building in southern France, the first such attack on the mainland in several years.
The Corsican National Liberation Front - Historical Wing (FLNC) said in a statement sent to local journalists that it carried out the attack but gave no further explanation.
The FLNC had recently threatened to carry its struggle to the mainland.
No one was hurt in the explosion in front of the law courts in the southern city of Aix-en-Provence early on Sunday, which damaged the facade and a ground-floor administrative office,
The same building was badly damaged in a November 1992 blast also claimed by Corsican separatists.
Militants on the French Mediterranean island have been waging a low-level guerrilla war for the past two decades in search of greater autonomy from mainland France.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has decreed a crackdown on separatist violence, but nationalist leaders have in turn accused him of burying secret talks aimed at resolving their differences.
